answer.generated: In RISC architectures, virtual memory serves as an intermediate level between real memory and physical memory, allowing the operating system to map virtual addresses to real addresses via page tables. Real memory is the actual physical storage where data resides, while physical memory refers to the hardware that holds the real memory. The VMM manages the mapping between virtual and physical memory, enabling multiple virtual address spaces per process. This hierarchy reduces fragmentation and improves protection by separating logical addresses from physical locations.
